description: Excel-style conditional formatting as a declarative engine prop of the Svelte 5 data grid. Pass every rule in one conditionalFormats array, later entries win, and no per-cell snippet is needed: dataBar draws a gradient-filled in-cell bar, colorScale paints heat maps as an alpha ramp, zero-centred, banded or compared against another column, iconSet adds arrows, traffic lights or triangles by threshold, and rule applies a style when a predicate matches. conditionalStatScope rescales the ramp to the visible rows.

faq.question: How do I add a heat map to a column?
faq.answer: Add { type: 'colorScale', columns: ['revenue'] } with min, mid and max colours to the conditionalFormats array. mode: 'alpha' with a base colour tints the cell with a translucent ramp that composites over zebra stripes and selection, and compareColumn scales one column against another.

faq.question: What does conditionalStatScope do?
faq.answer: It chooses whether min and max for a scale come from all rows or only the rows currently displayed. With 'visible', filtering the grid rescales the ramp to what is on screen; the demo toggles it live.

faq.question: How do rules combine?
faq.answer: Entries are applied in array order and later ones win for the same cell, so { type: 'rule' } with a predicate can sit on top of a colour scale for the same column, and { type: 'iconSet', columns: ['growth'], set: 'arrows', thresholds: [0, 10] } adds the icon without touching the fill.
